final_answer: Bottom coordinates: easting 5051.961524 m, northing 12090.000000 m, elevation 790.000000 m. Horizontal displacement: 103.923048 m. Trajectory deviation from vertical: 60°.
question_text: A drill hole collar is located at easting 5000.000 m, northing 12000.000 m, and elevation 850.000 m. The hole has an azimuth of 30° clockwise from north, a downward inclination of 30° from horizontal, and a drilled depth of 120.000 m. Calculate the bottom coordinates, horizontal displacement, and angular deviation from vertical, showing the calculation steps with units.
calculation_steps: 1. Horizontal displacement = depth × cos(inclination) = 120.000 m × cos(30°) = 103.923048 m. 2. Easting offset = horizontal displacement × sin(azimuth) = 103.923048 m × sin(30°) = 51.961524 m. 3. Northing offset = horizontal displacement × cos(azimuth) = 103.923048 m × cos(30°) = 90.000000 m. 4. Elevation change = −depth × sin(inclination) = −120.000 m × sin(30°) = −60.000000 m. 5. Bottom easting = 5000.000 m + 51.961524 m = 5051.961524 m; bottom northing = 12000.000 m + 90.000000 m = 12090.000000 m; bottom elevation = 850.000 m − 60.000000 m = 790.000000 m. 6. Trajectory deviation from vertical = 90° − 30° = 60°.
